tasks.task: Mobilise plant, scaffold and site setup
tasks.scope: Deliver scaffold materials to site. Establish laydown, storage, and welfare facilities in courtyard. Confirm access via Kiora Lane and courtyard. Set up signage and site boundaries.
hazards: vehicle collision — uncontrolled movement of delivery vehicles in courtyard with pedestrian and occupant traffic
struck by — falling or rolling scaffold materials during unloading and stacking
manual handling injury — lifting and moving heavy scaffold components without mechanical aid
trip hazard — scattered materials, cables and temporary structures obstructing access routes
tasks.dominant_hazard: vehicle collision with pedestrians or property
controls: Confirm access route via Kiora Lane is clear of parked vehicles, pedestrians, and overhead obstructions before delivery vehicle enters site.
Establish one-way vehicle flow through courtyard — entry via Kiora Lane only, exit marked and signed, no reversing permitted.
Station spotter at courtyard entry during all vehicle movements — radio communication with delivery driver, authority to stop vehicle immediately.
Unload scaffold materials only into designated laydown area — no unloading onto access routes or near building edge.
Use mechanical handling for bundles over 25 kg — no manual lifting of stacked or banded scaffold tubes or frames.
Stack scaffold materials on flat, stable ground — base levelled, no stacking on slope or uneven surface, bundles secured against roll.
Mark all temporary structures, cables, and material piles with hazard tape — maintain 1 m clear pedestrian corridor to all exits.
Confirm occupants and building management aware of delivery schedule — tell 24 hours before vehicle arrival.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start unloading until: access route surveyed by site supervisor and delivery vehicle fitted with reversing alarm and hazard beacons confirmed operational
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not store materials until: laydown area levelled, drained, and confirmed suitable by site supervisor for weight and stacking height
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start work until: written notification delivered to all affected occupants and body corporate/strata manager
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: vehicle enters courtyard without spotter, reversing occurs without authority, or pedestrian enters work zone during material handling
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold bundle shifts, rolls, or becomes unstable during unloading or stacking
🛑 STOP WORK if: access route becomes obstructed or trip hazard cannot be immediately cleared
admin: Obtain written confirmation from building management and occupants of access route and delivery schedule.
Provide delivery driver with site map, access restrictions, spotter contact details, and one-way flow diagram.
Brief all site personnel on vehicle movement restrictions and assembly point location before first delivery.
Record laydown area survey and material stacking approval in site diary.
Verify EPA licence held and copied to site before mobilisation.
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest — all personnel in courtyard during vehicle movement or material handling
Hard hat — all personnel in active work zone
steel-capped footwear— steel-capped boots — all personnel handling or near scaffold materials

monitoring.critical_control: Spotter confirms clear courtyard and authorises vehicle entry before each delivery movement.
monitoring.frequency: Before each vehicle entry and exit; continuous during unloading
monitoring.evidence: Spotter log with time, vehicle details, and clearance confirmation; photographic record of laydown area setup and material stacking

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold to balconies and work levels
tasks.scope: Erect working scaffold to all balcony levels requiring remedial works. make sure stability, guardrails, and edge protection. Document load capacity and bearing points. Confirm access ladders and landings.
hazards: fall from height — collapse or failure of erected scaffold due to inadequate base, bracing or load distribution
fall from height — worker falling from incomplete scaffold or during erection before guardrails installed
struck by — falling tools, fixings or scaffold components from height onto occupants below
instability — swaying or lateral movement of tall scaffold in wind or under load
bearing point failure — inadequate structural support or overloading of balcony slab at scaffold base points
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height — scaffold collapse or failure
controls: Obtain engineer-certified load calculation and bearing point schedule before scaffold erection starts — confirm balcony slab capacity at each base point and document maximum distributed load per point.
check base bearing surface (balcony slab) for cracks, spalling, or water damage — stop if structural damage is visible; document condition with dated photos.
Erect scaffold strictly to engineer detail and load calculations — use only approved scaffold components, correct member sizes, and specified bracing.
Install base plates and sole plates on level, clean bearing surfaces — make sure full contact with no gaps, shimming, or unsupported overhang.
Install guardrails (1.0–1.1 m height) and mid-rails (0.5 m height) on all open edges before workers access the scaffold — complete before any worker stands on platform.
Install catch nets or exclusion perimeter netting below scaffold to stop falling tools, fixings, and debris reaching occupants below.
Secure all loose components, tools, and materials to the scaffold — prohibit loose items on platforms.
Confirm access ladder is secured, correctly angled (70–75°), and extends 1.1 m above landing platform before any worker uses it.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start any worker access until: licenced scaffolder has completed erection, all guardrails and mid-rails are installed, base bearing points are inspected and approved by engineer or qualified person, and handover certificate is signed.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not load scaffold beyond documented maximum capacity until: engineer confirms all bracing, props, and load distribution paths are complete and undamaged.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component is visibly bent, cracked, or missing, or any bracing or diagonal member is loose or detached.
🛑 STOP WORK if: base plate or sole plate shifts, settles, or loses contact with bearing surface.
🛑 STOP WORK if: guardrail or mid-rail is damaged, incomplete, or cannot contain a worker at rest; or if exclusion netting tears or gaps appear.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and review engineer-certified load calculation and bearing point assessment before site mobilisation.
Confirm licenced scaffolder qualifications and current ticket before erection commences — record name, ticket number, and expiry date.
Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component is delivered to site.
Obtain handover certificate from licenced scaffolder before any worker access — keep on site and available for inspection.
Establish working at heights permit signed by site supervisor — confirm competency of all workers (current WHS induction, White Card, and working-at-heights competency verification).
Brief all workers on load capacity, bearing point locations, exclusion zones below, and wind speed limits before first access.
Record scaffold erection date, licenced scaffolder details, engineer, and handover sign-off in site logbook.
If balcony slab condition is uncertain, obtain structural engineer inspection before erection commences.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Fall-arrest harness and lanyard — anchor to permanent structure or approved scaffold anchor point when working at unprotected edges during erection or maintenance.

monitoring.critical_control: Licenced scaffolder visually confirms guardrails intact, bracing tight, base plates level and fully seated, and handover certificate signed before any worker access.
monitoring.frequency: Before first worker access, then daily pre-use, after wind events or structural disturbance
monitoring.evidence: Handover certificate signed and retained on site; daily pre-use checklist completed and dated; photos of bearing point condition and guardrail installation; engineer load calculation and bearing assessment on file.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing membrane, screed and tile bed
tasks.scope: Demolish and remove existing waterproofing membrane, screed layer and tile bed from balconies to structural slab. Load and remove all debris from site. Contain silica dust and manage damp removal.
hazards: silica dust inhalation — grinding, chipping and breaking of screed, tile and substrate generating respirable crystalline silica
manual handling injury — lifting and carrying heavy screed or tile material
eye injury — dust and debris without face protection
exposure to unknown hazardous materials — potential asbestos in adhesive, membrane or screed binder (latent condition)
tasks.dominant_hazard: silica dust inhalation — chronic lung disease risk
controls: Wet all surfaces with water mist before breaking out screed or tile — maintain damp state throughout removal — no dry breakout permitted
Use dust extraction shroud fitted to pneumatic chipping or grinding tool — extract dust at point of generation — test extraction before each shift start
Wear P2 respirator or half-mask with P2 cartridges — verify fit-tested size in personnel file — change cartridges each shift or when breathing resistance increases
Erect temporary polythene containment around work zone on balcony perimeter — seal gaps — prevent dust leaving occupied areas
Wear impact-resistant eye protection— wear chemical-resistant gloves during handling — wear steel-capped boots
Bag all broken tile and screed fragments in heavy-duty rubbish bags before transport — do not drop or throw debris — load into skip bin slowly to reduce dust release

Stop work immediately if asbestos-containing material is suspected — do not handle further — isolate area and tell Project Manager and WHS Advisor — await assessment by competent asbestos professional before continuing
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not break out screed or tile until: wet suppression system tested, dust extraction shroud inspected, and all workers have current P2 fit-test certificate and SDS briefing recorded
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove debris from balcony until: material sample checked and asbestos risk ruled out by WHS Advisor or competent asbestos professional
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails, surfaces dry out, or dry breakout occurs — re-wet and restart suppression before continuing
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction shroud becomes detached, blocked, or suction drops below audible level — repair or replace before resuming work
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is encountered or suspected — isolate area immediately
admin: Obtain EPA licence or confirmation of waste classification before transport
Verify scaffold erection permit and handover certificate current and signed by licenced scaffolder
Verify working at heights permit signed before each elevated shift
Confirm noise management plan in place and occupant notifications completed
Record pre-removal material check findings and asbestos risk assessment in project WHS file
Maintain daily log of dust extraction and wet suppression system function — sign off each shift
Arrange waste skip or licensed asbestos disposal contractor if asbestos confirmed
ppe: P2 respirator or half-mask with P2 cartridges — fit-tested to worker

monitoring.critical_control: Check wet suppression maintained and dust extraction suction audible before each break-out cycle
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during demolition; test extraction before shift start
monitoring.evidence: Daily wet suppression and extraction log signed by supervisor; dust extraction test record; P2 cartridge change log

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing membrane, screed and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing membrane, screed and per SWMS

tasks.task: Leo and Associates substrate inspection and approval
tasks.scope: Engage Leo and Associates to check exposed slab, cracks and substrate. Obtain written approval for repair method and extent before starting crack repairs. Record approval on site.
hazards: exposure to asbestos — disturbance of suspect asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive during inspector access and slab exposure (latent condition)
fall from height — inspector working at balcony edge during inspection without adequate edge protection
struck by — falling tools or materials during inspection work
tasks.dominant_hazard: exposure to asbestos during inspection (latent condition)
controls: Before Leo and Associates inspectors access the slab, confirm with building owner or manager whether the slab membrane or adhesive has been tested for asbestos. If unknown or untested, prohibit slab disturbance until asbestos testing is complete.

If asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive is confirmed or suspected, erect exclusion zone around slab exposure area. Restrict entry to Leo and Associates inspectors only. Post 'Danger — Asbestos' signage at all entry points.
Provide Leo and Associates with site-specific SDS for the membrane product before inspection starts. Confirm inspector has read and understood the SDS.

Install edge protection (guardrail or safety net) at all balcony edges where inspector will work. Minimum height 1100 mm, gap at toe 150 mm maximum. Check guardrail is secure and undamaged before inspector access.
Brief Leo and Associates inspector on balcony layout, exclusion zone boundary, and prohibited areas. need inspector to confirm understanding before starting work.

Prohibit inspector from working alone at balcony edge. Assign site supervisor or nominated worker to remain within visual line of sight during entire inspection. Supervisor must not use mobile phone or become distracted.
need inspector to move slowly, check footing before each step, and avoid carrying tools in hand over balcony edge. All tools must be secured in tool belt or lowered on lanyard.
Do not permit slab membrane or adhesive to be sampled, scraped, or disturbed during visual inspection. Visual assessment only unless Leo and Associates specifies otherwise in writing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start slab inspection until: asbestos status of membrane and adhesive is confirmed (tested or documented as unknown), edge protection is installed and checked, and Leo and Associates inspector confirms SDS has been reviewed
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack repair work until: written approval from Leo and Associates detailing repair method and extent is received, signed, and recorded on site
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive is disturbed, removed, or sampled during inspection
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is incomplete, damaged, or breached during inspection
🛑 STOP WORK if: Leo and Associates inspector works at balcony edge without supervisor in visual line of sight
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: make sure Leo and Associates holds current professional indemnity insurance. Request certificate of currency before site access.
Verify Leo and Associates inspector holds White Card (CPCCWHS1001) or equivalent construction induction. Request copy before work starts.

If scaffold is required for inspector access to balcony, obtain scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before erection starts. Obtain handover certificate before inspector uses scaffold.
If scaffold exceeds 4 m height, confirm scaffold design complies with WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.6 and load calculations are documented.

Obtain working at heights permit signed before inspector starts elevated work. Verify inspector holds current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per current RII Training Package).
Record inspection date, time, inspector name, and approval sign-off in site diary and project file.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before inspection starts and continuously during inspection
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry confirming edge protection check. Photographic record of installed guardrail. Supervisor sign-off on safety checklist.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Leo and Associates substrate inspection
responsibility.WKR: Perform Leo and Associates substrate inspection per SWMS

tasks.task: Repair slab cracks and defects
tasks.scope: Cut out cracks to prepared profile. Remove loose material. Apply concrete repair mortar or epoxy injection per engineer specification. Grind and finish level to slab surface.
hazards: silica dust inhalation — cutting, grinding and finishing concrete repair mortar generating respirable crystalline silica
chemical exposure — epoxy injection irritation or sensitisation to skin and respiratory system
struck by or caught — flying concrete or material fragments during cutting or grinding
eye injury — dust and particles without face protection
manual handling injury — moving and applying heavy repair mortar bags or injection cartridges
tasks.dominant_hazard: silica dust inhalation during crack repair grinding
controls: Use wet cutting method — spray water continuously during crack cutting to suppress dust at source.
Attach dust extraction unit to concrete grinder — HEPA filter, high-volume extractor running before and during all grinding.
Wear P2 or P3 respirator — fit-checked before start, replaced if damaged or wet.
Apply water misting or damp cloth to repair mortar surface before grinding — keep surface damp throughout finishing process.
Barricade work area — exclude non-essential occupants within 10 m radius during cutting and grinding.
Check grinder HEPA filter condition — replace if visibly loaded or suction drops.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves, apron and face shield — epoxy injection exposure when mixing or applying injection cartridges.
Obtain SDS for repair mortar or epoxy product — keep on site and brief all workers before application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not grind or finish repair mortar until: surface has been wetted and remains damp, dust extraction is running, and work area is barricaded to exclude occupants.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails or dust becomes visible airborne beyond barricade perimeter.
🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA dust extractor loses suction or filter requires replacement mid-task.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respirator becomes damp, damaged, or fit is lost.
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate is current and on site before elevated work starts.
Verify working at heights permit signed by authorised person before commencement.
Brief all workers on SDS for repair mortar and epoxy product — document attendance.
Confirm noise management plan is active — tell occupants of grinding schedule in advance.
Record HEPA filter replacement and grinder maintenance log on site.

monitoring.critical_control: Wet suppression running and visible at cutting and grinding point; HEPA dust extractor suction confirmed before each task.
monitoring.frequency: Before cutting starts; continuously during grinding; check HEPA filter condition each shift and after 4 hours grinding.
monitoring.evidence: Water misting visible at work point; dust extractor running light on and hose pressure confirmed; HEPA filter inspection log with date and worker signature.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Apply new waterproofing membrane system
tasks.scope: Prepare and prime slab surface. Apply new liquid or sheet waterproofing membrane system per product specification. Include all joints, penetrations and upstands. Confirm full coverage and curing time.
hazards: chemical burn or irritation — contact with liquid waterproofing chemicals or primers on skin or eyes
inhalation of fumes — application of liquid membrane or primer in enclosed balcony space without adequate ventilation
slip hazard — wet or damp membrane material on slab surface creating slip risk for workers at height
inadequate curing — premature foot traffic or weather exposure before membrane cure time compromising waterproofing integrity
tasks.dominant_hazard: chemical inhalation from membrane application in confined balcony space
controls: Obtain SDS for membrane product and primer before work starts. Keep SDS on point of use always.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation in balcony space before application. Measure air velocity — minimum 0.5 m/s at work face. Stop work if ventilation fails.
check substrate for contamination, dampness, or existing damage before priming. Record findings. Do not prime if substrate is wet or contaminated.
Apply primer per product SDS — use recommended coverage rate and drying time between coats. Do not skip primer stage.
Apply membrane system per product specification — thickness, overlap, temperature, humidity window. Record application conditions and batch numbers.
Mark all joints, penetrations and upstands with visible line before membrane application. Verify full coverage after application using visual check and touch test.
Establish wet surface exclusion zone around freshly applied membrane. Place wet-floor signs and barriers to restrict foot traffic.
Confirm cure time from SDS. Do not allow foot traffic or weather exposure until cure time is met. Record cure completion sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: substrate is dry, clean, primed and inspector has verified fitness for application
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or weather exposure until: cure time specified on SDS has been confirmed and recorded
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical ventilation fails or air velocity falls below 0.5 m/s
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition changes (water ingress, contamination, or frost risk) during or before application
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions exceed product temperature or humidity limits specified on SDS
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain SDS training certificate for membrane product and primer before application. All workers on task must be briefed on SDS contents and hazard controls.
Confirm scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses elevated work area.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by supervisor before elevated application commences.
Record substrate condition, ventilation readings, membrane batch numbers, application conditions, and cure time sign-off on daily log.
tell building occupants of chemical application in progress and ventilation activity. Post 'Do not enter' signage at balcony access.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
ppe: Respiratory protective equipment — APF 5 half-mask respirator with organic vapour and particulate cartridges (if mechanical ventilation cannot be confirmed or fails)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify mechanical ventilation air velocity minimum 0.5 m/s at work face using anemometer before application starts and continuously during work.
monitoring.frequency: Before application commences, every 30 minutes during application, immediately after any ventilation system adjustment
monitoring.evidence: Anemometer reading recorded on daily log. Ventilation system inspection tag current and visible.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Apply new waterproofing membrane system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply new waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

tasks.task: Install screed and new tile bed system
tasks.scope: Apply substrate primer and tile adhesive bed to waterproofed slab. Install new tiles to balcony surface. Grout joints and cure per specification. Install drainage and edge details.
hazards: dust generation — mixing and application of tile adhesive and substrate primer generating inhalation risk
manual handling injury — lifting and carrying heavy tile materials and adhesive bags
chemical exposure — tile adhesive skin contact or inhalation
slip hazard — wet adhesive on slab at height creating slip and fall risk
heat stress — working in direct sun on exposed balcony during adhesive application and cure
tasks.dominant_hazard: slip hazard on wet adhesive at height
controls: Apply substrate primer to waterproofed slab according to product SDS; make sure substrate is clean, dry, and free of dust before application.
Mix tile adhesive in sealed mixer or pre-mixed; prohibit dry powder mixing on slab — bag dust creates inhalation risk at height.
Ventilate adhesive fumes continuously during application — open scaffolding access, no enclosure that traps vapour.
Lay anti-slip surface or absorbent mat on wet adhesive zones to prevent slip during tile placement; replace mat before each new adhesive batch.
Install edge barriers or handrails around balcony perimeter before adhesive application starts — prevent step-off or tool drop.
Restrict worker numbers on slab to essential personnel only — reduce load, reduce crowding, reduce slip risk on wet surface.
Lift and carry adhesive bags and tiles using correct manual handling — bend knees, straight back, two-person lift for bags over 15 kg.
Wear respirator (P2 minimum) during primer mixing and adhesive application if SDS states inhalation hazard.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: substrate is checked dry, clean, and free of dust by supervisor, and ambient temperature is within product SDS limits.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile laying until: substrate primer has cured per product SDS and adhesive bed temperature is checked compliant with cure window specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet adhesive is exposed without anti-slip mat or weather changes within cure window (rain forecast, frost risk, temperature drop below SDS minimum).
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker shows signs of heat stress (confusion, dizziness, weakness) or adverse skin reaction to adhesive.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffolding condition changes (visible movement, loose boards, missing handrails) or handover certificate cannot be produced on demand.
admin: Verify scaffolding handover certificate is signed by licensed scaffolder and dated before work start — file on site.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and current before elevated task commences.
Obtain SDS for substrate primer and tile adhesive; keep on point of use during mixing and application.
Brief all workers on slip hazard at height, adhesive hazards, and heat stress prevention before slab work starts.
Record all workers on slab, time of entry and exit, and any adverse events or near-hits during cure phase.
Confirm noise management plan addresses impact on occupied residential units below during mixing, application, and grouting.
Verify all workers hold current White Card and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E equivalent); check cards before work.
make sure debris and spillage from adhesive mixing are contained and removed from slab daily — prevent slip hazard from next-day work.
ppe: Safety helmet with chin strap (wind exposure at height)
Respirator P2 minimum during primer mixing and adhesive application (if SDS specifies inhalation hazard)
Steel-capped boots with non-slip sole (slip hazard on wet adhesive)
High-visibility vest (occupied building — prevent contact with other workers or occupants on adjacent areas)

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.who: Supervisor continuous observation; workers self-check before each step.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during adhesive application and tile laying; every 30 minutes during cure phase for heat stress check.
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of mat in place; no slips or near-slips recorded; no worker remains on slab longer than 30 minutes in direct sun; SDS and handover certificate sighted and dated on site.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Install screed and new tile
responsibility.WKR: Perform Install screed and new tile per SWMS

tasks.task: Isolate and protect occupant spaces below balconies
tasks.scope: Install sheeting, barriers and exclusion zones to prevent debris fall onto occupied residential areas and courtyard. Establish no-entry signage and barricades.
hazards: debris fall — inadequate or failed sheeting allowing fragments to fall onto occupants or courtyard below
struck by — heavy sheeting coming loose in wind and striking pedestrians
entanglement or trapped limb — loose sheeting material catching on occupants or temporary structures
inadequate warning — missing or obscured signage resulting in occupant entry into exclusion zone
controls: Install horizontal debris netting or solid sheeting to full width and depth of balcony overhang before any work commences at height above occupied areas.
Secure all sheeting with mechanical fixings at maximum 1 m centres; verify no gaps, tears, or loose edges exist before occupancy resumes below.
Establish ground-level exclusion zone directly below balcony work extending minimum 2 m from facade; barricade with standard construction barriers.
Install and maintain high-visibility 'No Entry' signage at all entry points to exclusion zone in English and resident language where applicable.
Check sheeting and fixings daily before work starts and after wind speeds exceed 15 km/h or adverse weather events.
Brief all site personnel and occupants on exclusion zone boundaries, entry prohibition, and debris fall risk before work commences.
Remove or secure all loose debris from scaffold platforms and ledges daily; do not allow accumulation above 100 mm depth.
Conduct visual check of sheeting integrity from ground level each shift start; report and repair any damage, gaps, or movement immediately.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start elevated work until: sheeting installation is complete, all fixings are tight, no gaps or tears exist, and licensed scaffolder has signed handover certificate.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: sheeting develops tears, gaps, or loosens; fixings loosen or pull free; wind exceeds 20 km/h sustained or gusts exceed 25 km/h.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant or unauthorised person enters exclusion zone; signage is missing, obscured, or illegible.
🛑 STOP WORK if: debris accumulates on sheeting or scaffold above exclusion zone and cannot be safely removed without compromising containment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain scaffold erection permit signed by licensed scaffolder before scaffold assembly.
Obtain working at heights permit signed before each elevated task commences.
Obtain scaffold handover certificate from licensed scaffolder before any worker uses scaffold.
Confirm all site personnel hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) or equivalent.
Confirm all personnel working at height hold current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per current RII Training Package).
Confirm scaffolder holds appropriate licence for scaffold class and height.
Provide SDS training to all personnel handling sheeting membrane product on point of use.
tell building occupants in writing of exclusion zone boundaries, duration, and no-entry requirement before work starts.
Maintain daily log of exclusion zone patrols and sheeting condition checks; record any defects and remedial action.
Conduct toolbox talk on debris fall risk, exclusion zone entry prohibition, and emergency response before each work day.
ppe: Hard hat with chin strap (elevated work)
High-visibility vest or Class D reflective clothing
steel-capped footwear, slip-resistant, minimum sole thickness 6 mm)
Harness and lanyard (when working at height above 2 m; tethered to secure anchor point rated for load)

monitoring.critical_control: Check sheeting fixings and debris containment integrity each shift start and after weather events.
monitoring.frequency: Before each shift start, after wind events, after adverse weather, daily during work
monitoring.evidence: Signed daily checklist recording sheeting condition, fixings integrity, exclusion zone status, signage presence, occupant compliance; photographs of any defects; work log of remedial actions taken

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Isolate and protect occupant spaces
responsibility.WKR: Perform Isolate and protect occupant spaces per SWMS

tasks.task: Investigate and expose slab surface
tasks.scope: Sweep and clean slab surface. Mark and expose all visible cracks. Document crack patterns, width and depth. Confirm substrate condition ready for inspection hold point.
hazards: dust generation — sweeping and wire-brushing exposed concrete generating dust inhalation risk
sharp edges or protrusions — exposed slab cracks and rough concrete creating cut or laceration risk
fall hazard — working on uneven or broken slab surface at height
eye injury — dust particles without eye protection
controls: Wet sweep slab surface using low-pressure water spray to suppress dust before dry cleaning starts.
Wear disposable dust mask (P2 or P3 rated) fitted and sealed during all sweeping and brushing work.
Use wet wire brush or damp cloth to clean cracks — do not dry brush or grind exposed concrete.
Wear eye protection
Mark all visible cracks with chalk or pen — do not re-strike or enlarge cracks during marking.
Measure crack width using calliper or ruler; record depth by visual assessment or probe — do not force probes into tight cracks.
Photograph crack pattern and documentation before proceeding — use consistent lighting and scale reference.
Brief all workers on uneven slab surface hazards and no-run zones — point out trip edges and protrusions before work starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to structural assessment until: slab surface is cleaned, all visible cracks are marked and measured, crack pattern is documented with photographs, and substrate condition is confirmed ready for inspection by [named structural engineer or project supervisor].
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet dust suppression fails, is turned off, or cannot be maintained during cleaning.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unexpected substrate condition is found — delamination, spalling, or hidden voids — until engineer confirms method can proceed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: workers are observed working without fitted dust mask or eye protection
admin: Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) induction and working at heights competency before task starts.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed and on site before slab access commences.
Brief occupants on dust suppression and water runoff — confirm containment method is acceptable before starting.
Record all crack measurements, photographs, and substrate condition assessment in site diary and attach to inspection report.
tell site supervisor of any unexpected findings — material change, repair patches, or structural movement — before proceeding.
ppe: Disposable dust mask P2 or P3 (fitted and sealed)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Continuous throughout slab cleaning; check before each sweeping pass and at shift start.
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of damp slab surface; water spray visible and active; worker's dust mask remains clean and unblocked throughout task; no visible dust clouds during work.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Investigate and expose slab surface
responsibility.WKR: Perform Investigate and expose slab surface per SWMS

tasks.task: Reinstate balustrades and fittings
tasks.scope: Reset and secure balustrades, handrails and edge protection to finished height. Reinstall planters, vents, penetrations and service sleeves. make sure all fixings are secure and compliant.
hazards: fall from height — working at balcony edge without guardrails during balustrade removal and reinstatement
struck by — falling balustrade components or tools during removal or installation
manual handling injury — lifting and positioning heavy balustrade panels or support frames
inadequate fixings — balustrade installed without proper anchoring creating fall hazard for building occupants
tasks.dominant_hazard: fall from height during balustrade work at edge
controls: Install edge protection or safety barriers before removing existing balustrades — no work at unprotected edge.
Use scaffolding or certified elevated work platform with guardrails for all work above 2 m — harness-on-lanyard only if platform guardrails fail inspection.
check all balustrade fixings with torque wrench before final sign-off — confirm all bolts meet engineer specification.
Secure each balustrade panel to structural support using certified fixings — no improvisation or substitution of bolt grade.
Use two workers minimum for lifting panels over 20 kg — mechanical hoist for panels over 30 kg.
Contain all removed balustrade components and fixings in designated drop zone — no casting down to lower levels.
Check structural support and attachment points for damage or corrosion before reinstalling balustrades — photograph and report defects to supervisor.
Verify weather window — stop work if rain, wind over 30 km/h, or frost forecast within 24 hours of silicone or sealant application.

tasks.scope: Apply substrate primer and tile adhesive bed to waterproofed slab. Install new tiles to balcony surface. Grout joints and cure per specification. Install drainage and edge details.

tasks.task: Reinstate balustrades and fittings
tasks.scope: Reset and secure balustrades, handrails and edge protection to finished height. Reinstall planters, vents, penetrations and service sleeves. Ensure all fixings are secure and compliant.

task_blocks_raw.task: Isolate and protect occupant spaces below balconies
task_blocks_raw.scope: Install sheeting, barriers and exclusion zones to prevent debris fall onto occupied residential areas and courtyard. Establish no-entry signage and barricades.
hazards: debris fall — inadequate or failed sheeting allowing fragments to fall onto occupants or courtyard below
struck by — heavy sheeting coming loose in wind and striking pedestrians
entanglement or trapped limb — loose sheeting material catching on occupants or temporary structures
inadequate warning — missing or obscured signage resulting in occupant entry into exclusion zone
controls: Install horizontal debris netting or solid sheeting to full width and depth of balcony overhang before any work commences at height above occupied areas.
Secure all sheeting with mechanical fixings at maximum 1 m centres; verify no gaps, tears, or loose edges exist before occupancy resumes below.
Establish ground-level exclusion zone directly below balcony work extending minimum 2 m from facade; barricade with standard construction barriers.
Install and maintain high-visibility 'No Entry' signage at all entry points to exclusion zone in English and resident language where applicable.
Check sheeting and fixings daily before work starts and after wind speeds exceed 15 km/h or adverse weather events.
Brief all site personnel and occupants on exclusion zone boundaries, entry prohibition, and debris fall risk before work commences.
Remove or secure all loose debris from scaffold platforms and ledges daily; do not allow accumulation above 100 mm depth.
Conduct visual check of sheeting integrity from ground level each shift start; report and repair any damage, gaps, or movement immediately.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start elevated work until: sheeting installation is complete, all fixings are tight, no gaps or tears exist, and licensed scaffolder has signed handover certificate.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: sheeting develops tears, gaps, or loosens; fixings loosen or pull free; wind exceeds 20 km/h sustained or gusts exceed 25 km/h.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant or unauthorised person enters exclusion zone; signage is missing, obscured, or illegible.
🛑 STOP WORK if: debris accumulates on sheeting or scaffold above exclusion zone and cannot be safely removed without compromising containment.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

task_blocks_raw.task: Remove existing membrane, screed and tile bed

hazards: silica dust inhalation — grinding, chipping and breaking of screed, tile and substrate generating respirable crystalline silica
manual handling injury — lifting and carrying heavy screed or tile material
eye injury — dust and debris without face protection
exposure to unknown hazardous materials — potential asbestos in adhesive, membrane or screed binder (latent condition)
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: silica dust inhalation — chronic lung disease risk
controls: Wet all surfaces with water mist before breaking out screed or tile — maintain damp state throughout removal — no dry breakout permitted
Use dust extraction shroud fitted to pneumatic chipping or grinding tool — extract dust at point of generation — test extraction before each shift start
Wear P2 respirator or half-mask with P2 cartridges — verify fit-tested size in personnel file — change cartridges each shift or when breathing resistance increases
Erect temporary polythene containment around work zone on balcony perimeter — seal gaps — prevent dust leaving occupied areas
Wear impact-resistant eye protection— wear chemical-resistant gloves during handling — wear steel-capped boots
Bag all broken tile and screed fragments in heavy-duty rubbish bags before transport — do not drop or throw debris — load into skip bin slowly to reduce dust release

Stop work immediately if asbestos-containing material is suspected — do not handle further — isolate area and tell Project Manager and WHS Advisor — await assessment by competent asbestos professional before continuing

⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not remove debris from balcony until: material sample checked and asbestos risk ruled out by WHS Advisor or competent asbestos professional
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails, surfaces dry out, or dry breakout occurs — re-wet and restart suppression before continuing
🛑 STOP WORK if: dust extraction shroud becomes detached, blocked, or suction drops below audible level — repair or replace before resuming work
🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing material is encountered or suspected — isolate area immediately

task_blocks_raw.scope: Sweep and clean slab surface. Mark and expose all visible cracks. Document crack patterns, width and depth. Confirm substrate condition ready for inspection hold point.
hazards: dust generation — sweeping and wire-brushing exposed concrete generating dust inhalation risk
sharp edges or protrusions — exposed slab cracks and rough concrete creating cut or laceration risk
fall hazard — working on uneven or broken slab surface at height
eye injury — dust particles without eye protection
controls: Wet sweep slab surface using low-pressure water spray to suppress dust before dry cleaning starts.
Wear disposable dust mask (P2 or P3 rated) fitted and sealed during all sweeping and brushing work.
Use wet wire brush or damp cloth to clean cracks — do not dry brush or grind exposed concrete.
Wear eye protection
Mark all visible cracks with chalk or pen — do not re-strike or enlarge cracks during marking.
Measure crack width using calliper or ruler; record depth by visual assessment or probe — do not force probes into tight cracks.
Photograph crack pattern and documentation before proceeding — use consistent lighting and scale reference.
Brief all workers on uneven slab surface hazards and no-run zones — point out trip edges and protrusions before work starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to structural assessment until: slab surface is cleaned, all visible cracks are marked and measured, crack pattern is documented with photographs, and substrate condition is confirmed ready for inspection by [named structural engineer or project supervisor].
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet dust suppression fails, is turned off, or cannot be maintained during cleaning.
🛑 STOP WORK if: unexpected substrate condition is found — delamination, spalling, or hidden voids — until engineer confirms method can proceed.
🛑 STOP WORK if: workers are observed working without fitted dust mask or eye protection
admin: Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) induction and working at heights competency before task starts.
Confirm scaffold handover certificate is signed and on site before slab access commences.
Brief occupants on dust suppression and water runoff — confirm containment method is acceptable before starting.
Record all crack measurements, photographs, and substrate condition assessment in site diary and attach to inspection report.
tell site supervisor of any unexpected findings — material change, repair patches, or structural movement — before proceeding.
ppe: Disposable dust mask P2 or P3 (fitted and sealed)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Continuous throughout slab cleaning; check before each sweeping pass and at shift start.
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of damp slab surface; water spray visible and active; worker's dust mask remains clean and unblocked throughout task; no visible dust clouds during work.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Investigate and expose slab surface
responsibility.WKR: Perform Investigate and expose slab surface per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.task: Leo and Associates substrate inspection and approval
task_blocks_raw.scope: Engage Leo and Associates to check exposed slab, cracks and substrate. Obtain written approval for repair method and extent before starting crack repairs. Record approval on site.
hazards: exposure to asbestos — disturbance of suspect asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive during inspector access and slab exposure (latent condition)
fall from height — inspector working at balcony edge during inspection without adequate edge protection
struck by — falling tools or materials during inspection work
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: exposure to asbestos during inspection (latent condition)
controls: Before Leo and Associates inspectors access the slab, confirm with building owner or manager whether the slab membrane or adhesive has been tested for asbestos. If unknown or untested, prohibit slab disturbance until asbestos testing is complete.

If asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive is confirmed or suspected, erect exclusion zone around slab exposure area. Restrict entry to Leo and Associates inspectors only. Post 'Danger — Asbestos' signage at all entry points.
Provide Leo and Associates with site-specific SDS for the membrane product before inspection starts. Confirm inspector has read and understood the SDS.

Install edge protection (guardrail or safety net) at all balcony edges where inspector will work. Minimum height 1100 mm, gap at toe 150 mm maximum. Check guardrail is secure and undamaged before inspector access.
Brief Leo and Associates inspector on balcony layout, exclusion zone boundary, and prohibited areas. need inspector to confirm understanding before starting work.

Prohibit inspector from working alone at balcony edge. Assign site supervisor or nominated worker to remain within visual line of sight during entire inspection. Supervisor must not use mobile phone or become distracted.
need inspector to move slowly, check footing before each step, and avoid carrying tools in hand over balcony edge. All tools must be secured in tool belt or lowered on lanyard.
Do not permit slab membrane or adhesive to be sampled, scraped, or disturbed during visual inspection. Visual assessment only unless Leo and Associates specifies otherwise in writing.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start slab inspection until: asbestos status of membrane and adhesive is confirmed (tested or documented as unknown), edge protection is installed and checked, and Leo and Associates inspector confirms SDS has been reviewed
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start crack repair work until: written approval from Leo and Associates detailing repair method and extent is received, signed, and recorded on site
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: asbestos-containing membrane or adhesive is disturbed, removed, or sampled during inspection
🛑 STOP WORK if: edge protection is incomplete, damaged, or breached during inspection
🛑 STOP WORK if: Leo and Associates inspector works at balcony edge without supervisor in visual line of sight
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

If scaffold exceeds 4 m height, confirm scaffold design complies with WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.6 and load calculations are documented.

Obtain working at heights permit signed before inspector starts elevated work. Verify inspector holds current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per current RII Training Package).
Record inspection date, time, inspector name, and approval sign-off in site diary and project file.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: Before inspection starts and continuously during inspection
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry confirming edge protection check. Photographic record of installed guardrail. Supervisor sign-off on safety checklist.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Leo and Associates substrate inspection
responsibility.WKR: Perform Leo and Associates substrate inspection per SWMS

task_blocks_raw.scope: Cut out cracks to prepared profile. Remove loose material. Apply concrete repair mortar or epoxy injection per engineer specification. Grind and finish level to slab surface.
hazards: silica dust inhalation — cutting, grinding and finishing concrete repair mortar generating respirable crystalline silica
chemical exposure — epoxy injection irritation or sensitisation to skin and respiratory system
struck by or caught — flying concrete or material fragments during cutting or grinding
eye injury — dust and particles without face protection
manual handling injury — moving and applying heavy repair mortar bags or injection cartridges
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: silica dust inhalation during crack repair grinding
controls: Use wet cutting method — spray water continuously during crack cutting to suppress dust at source.
Attach dust extraction unit to concrete grinder — HEPA filter, high-volume extractor running before and during all grinding.
Wear P2 or P3 respirator — fit-checked before start, replaced if damaged or wet.
Apply water misting or damp cloth to repair mortar surface before grinding — keep surface damp throughout finishing process.
Barricade work area — exclude non-essential occupants within 10 m radius during cutting and grinding.
Check grinder HEPA filter condition — replace if visibly loaded or suction drops.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves, apron and face shield — epoxy injection exposure when mixing or applying injection cartridges.
Obtain SDS for repair mortar or epoxy product — keep on site and brief all workers before application.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not grind or finish repair mortar until: surface has been wetted and remains damp, dust extraction is running, and work area is barricaded to exclude occupants.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet suppression fails or dust becomes visible airborne beyond barricade perimeter.
🛑 STOP WORK if: HEPA dust extractor loses suction or filter requires replacement mid-task.
🛑 STOP WORK if: respirator becomes damp, damaged, or fit is lost.
admin: Confirm scaffold handover certificate is current and on site before elevated work starts.
Verify working at heights permit signed by authorised person before commencement.
Brief all workers on SDS for repair mortar and epoxy product — document attendance.
Confirm noise management plan is active — tell occupants of grinding schedule in advance.
Record HEPA filter replacement and grinder maintenance log on site.

monitoring.critical_control: Wet suppression running and visible at cutting and grinding point; HEPA dust extractor suction confirmed before each task.
monitoring.frequency: Before cutting starts; continuously during grinding; check HEPA filter condition each shift and after 4 hours grinding.
monitoring.evidence: Water misting visible at work point; dust extractor running light on and hose pressure confirmed; HEPA filter inspection log with date and worker signature.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

task_blocks_raw.scope: Prepare and prime slab surface. Apply new liquid or sheet waterproofing membrane system per product specification. Include all joints, penetrations and upstands. Confirm full coverage and curing time.
hazards: chemical burn or irritation — contact with liquid waterproofing chemicals or primers on skin or eyes
inhalation of fumes — application of liquid membrane or primer in enclosed balcony space without adequate ventilation
slip hazard — wet or damp membrane material on slab surface creating slip risk for workers at height
inadequate curing — premature foot traffic or weather exposure before membrane cure time compromising waterproofing integrity
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: chemical inhalation from membrane application in confined balcony space
controls: Obtain SDS for membrane product and primer before work starts. Keep SDS on point of use always.
Establish continuous mechanical ventilation in balcony space before application. Measure air velocity — minimum 0.5 m/s at work face. Stop work if ventilation fails.
check substrate for contamination, dampness, or existing damage before priming. Record findings. Do not prime if substrate is wet or contaminated.
Apply primer per product SDS — use recommended coverage rate and drying time between coats. Do not skip primer stage.
Apply membrane system per product specification — thickness, overlap, temperature, humidity window. Record application conditions and batch numbers.
Mark all joints, penetrations and upstands with visible line before membrane application. Verify full coverage after application using visual check and touch test.
Establish wet surface exclusion zone around freshly applied membrane. Place wet-floor signs and barriers to restrict foot traffic.
Confirm cure time from SDS. Do not allow foot traffic or weather exposure until cure time is met. Record cure completion sign-off.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: substrate is dry, clean, primed and inspector has verified fitness for application
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow foot traffic or weather exposure until: cure time specified on SDS has been confirmed and recorded
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: mechanical ventilation fails or air velocity falls below 0.5 m/s
🛑 STOP WORK if: substrate condition changes (water ingress, contamination, or frost risk) during or before application
🛑 STOP WORK if: weather conditions exceed product temperature or humidity limits specified on SDS
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded

tell building occupants of chemical application in progress and ventilation activity. Post 'Do not enter' signage at balcony access.

task_blocks_raw.task: Install screed and new tile bed system
task_blocks_raw.scope: Apply substrate primer and tile adhesive bed to waterproofed slab. Install new tiles to balcony surface. Grout joints and cure per specification. Install drainage and edge details.
hazards: dust generation — mixing and application of tile adhesive and substrate primer generating inhalation risk
manual handling injury — lifting and carrying heavy tile materials and adhesive bags
chemical exposure — tile adhesive skin contact or inhalation
slip hazard — wet adhesive on slab at height creating slip and fall risk
heat stress — working in direct sun on exposed balcony during adhesive application and cure
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: slip hazard on wet adhesive at height
controls: Apply substrate primer to waterproofed slab according to product SDS; make sure substrate is clean, dry, and free of dust before application.
Mix tile adhesive in sealed mixer or pre-mixed; prohibit dry powder mixing on slab — bag dust creates inhalation risk at height.
Ventilate adhesive fumes continuously during application — open scaffolding access, no enclosure that traps vapour.
Lay anti-slip surface or absorbent mat on wet adhesive zones to prevent slip during tile placement; replace mat before each new adhesive batch.
Install edge barriers or handrails around balcony perimeter before adhesive application starts — prevent step-off or tool drop.
Restrict worker numbers on slab to essential personnel only — reduce load, reduce crowding, reduce slip risk on wet surface.
Lift and carry adhesive bags and tiles using correct manual handling — bend knees, straight back, two-person lift for bags over 15 kg.
Wear respirator (P2 minimum) during primer mixing and adhesive application if SDS states inhalation hazard.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply primer until: substrate is checked dry, clean, and free of dust by supervisor, and ambient temperature is within product SDS limits.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile laying until: substrate primer has cured per product SDS and adhesive bed temperature is checked compliant with cure window specification.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wet adhesive is exposed without anti-slip mat or weather changes within cure window (rain forecast, frost risk, temperature drop below SDS minimum).
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker shows signs of heat stress (confusion, dizziness, weakness) or adverse skin reaction to adhesive.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffolding condition changes (visible movement, loose boards, missing handrails) or handover certificate cannot be produced on demand.
admin: Verify scaffolding handover certificate is signed by licensed scaffolder and dated before work start — file on site.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and current before elevated task commences.
Obtain SDS for substrate primer and tile adhesive; keep on point of use during mixing and application.
Brief all workers on slip hazard at height, adhesive hazards, and heat stress prevention before slab work starts.
Record all workers on slab, time of entry and exit, and any adverse events or near-hits during cure phase.
Confirm noise management plan addresses impact on occupied residential units below during mixing, application, and grouting.
Verify all workers hold current White Card and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E equivalent); check cards before work.
make sure debris and spillage from adhesive mixing are contained and removed from slab daily — prevent slip hazard from next-day work.

Respirator P2 minimum during primer mixing and adhesive application (if SDS specifies inhalation hazard)
Steel-capped boots with non-slip sole (slip hazard on wet adhesive)
High-visibility vest (occupied building — prevent contact with other workers or occupants on adjacent areas)

struck by — falling balustrade components or tools during removal or installation
manual handling injury — lifting and positioning heavy balustrade panels or support frames
inadequate fixings — balustrade installed without proper anchoring creating fall hazard for building occupants

Use scaffolding or certified elevated work platform with guardrails for all work above 2 m — harness-on-lanyard only if platform guardrails fail inspection.
check all balustrade fixings with torque wrench before final sign-off — confirm all bolts meet engineer specification.
Secure each balustrade panel to structural support using certified fixings — no improvisation or substitution of bolt grade.
Use two workers minimum for lifting panels over 20 kg — mechanical hoist for panels over 30 kg.
Contain all removed balustrade components and fixings in designated drop zone — no casting down to lower levels.
Check structural support and attachment points for damage or corrosion before reinstalling balustrades — photograph and report defects to supervisor.
Verify weather window — stop work if rain, wind over 30 km/h, or frost forecast within 24 hours of silicone or sealant application.

task_blocks_raw.scope: Dismantle working scaffold from all levels. Remove all plant, materials and debris from site. Clean courtyard and Kiora Lane. Restore site to original condition.
hazards: fall from height — worker falling during scaffold dismantling before lower sections are protected
struck by — falling scaffold components or fixings onto occupants below or site personnel
crushing injury — scaffold components failing or collapsing during removal
manual handling injury — heavy scaffold parts requiring lifting during removal and loading
vehicle collision — uncontrolled movement of delivery vehicles during debris removal in courtyard
task_blocks_raw.dominant_hazard: fall from height during scaffold dismantling
controls: Obtain signed scaffold dismantling plan from licenced scaffolder before any dismantling starts. Plan must identify sequence, prop removal order, and fall protection for each level.
Erect and maintain full perimeter exclusion zone (minimum 1.5 m beyond scaffold base). Prohibit all unauthorised entry. Position warning signs at each access point.
Do not dismantle scaffold until upper levels are fully protected by completed lower levels or certified hard edge protection. Work top-down only.
Wear correctly fitted harness and lanyard clipped to certified anchor point before accessing or working on scaffold at height. check harness and lanyard before each use.
Use certified manual handling equipment (hoist, gin wheel, or mobile elevated work platform) for all scaffold components exceeding 20 kg. Do not hand-lower heavy sections.
Establish continuous communication (radio or phone) between scaffold dismantler(s) and ground spotters. Spotters must maintain visual contact and clear exclusion zone.
Place debris nets or catch barriers beneath dismantling work to contain falling fixings, clips, and small components.
Stop dismantling immediately if wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or if weather deteriorates. Do not resume until conditions are safe.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not dismantle any scaffold section until: licensed scaffolder has signed off dismantling plan and specified sequence is confirmed on site
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start debris removal by vehicle until: exclusion zone is confirmed clear of personnel and occupants are notified of truck movements
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component shows signs of damage, cracking, or instability during dismantling
🛑 STOP WORK if: a worker attempts to dismantle upper levels before lower levels are protected or harness cannot be secured to a certified anchor
🛑 STOP WORK if: exclusion zone is breached by occupants, vehicles, or unauthorised personnel
admin: Confirm all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and applicable scaffolding licence before work starts.
Verify working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent) is current for all personnel at height.
Obtain written confirmation from occupants that alternative access routes are in place before scaffold removal.
Record all scaffold defects found during dismantling in site diary and report to project manager immediately.
Maintain scaffold dismantling plan and signed handover certificate on site throughout demobilisation.
Provide induction to all demobilisation workers covering hazards, exclusion zones, emergency procedures, and occupant contact protocols.
ppe: Hard hat — worn always on site
High-visibility vest — visible from all angles
Safety harness and lanyard — correctly fitted and clipped before accessing scaffold at height
Eye protection — clear or tinted as weather requires

monitoring.critical_control: Check harness and anchor point secured before each worker accesses scaffold. Verify exclusion zone is maintained and clear of all unauthorised personnel.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous — before each worker ascends | each debris removal vehicle movement | after any weather change
monitoring.evidence: Site diary entry confirming harness check and anchor point verification | Exclusion zone sign-in log | Photos of protected edges before dismantling each level | Signed dismantling plan sections completed

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues
